items.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: But on one of the records I did with him – it might have been Naima – it was direct-to-disc.

ctx.x: I have a recording where he did something for Rosa Parks, and it was under a different name. But that was very recent, very very recent.

He did call me maybe two or three years ago about doing something. I never did get to talk to him, whatever it was. But yeah, that was – he was very different, very ambitious, in terms of big works, things like that. But on one of the records I did with him – it might have been Naima – it was direct-to-disc. That was unusual, because you couldn’t stop. It wasn’t like, okay, one tune, next tune. No, this, you had to go all the way through. So Naima is the whole track, because it was an LP. So that’s the only song…
The Angels of Atlanta is probably another extended work.
